strings.This is a general harmonic template. It: This is a general harmonic template. It is not a transcription of any particular song, and the app never claims that a specific song uses exactly the chords shown.
strings.Three major chords plus the relative min: Three major chords plus the relative minor vi, which adds a touch of melancholy to the major-key loop.
strings.Starts on the minor vi, which gives the: Starts on the minor vi, which gives the loop a more serious, bittersweet character; no strong V–I closure.
strings.Same four chords as the axis loop in a d: Same four chords as the axis loop in a different order; the final V pulls strongly back to I.
strings.Opens on the subdominant for a lifting,: Opens on the subdominant for a lifting, unexpected start; the vi at the end avoids a full cadence.
strings.Pure primary chords; the IV–I plagal mot: Pure primary chords; the IV–I plagal motion gives a relaxed, open feel.
strings.The classic three-chord cadence: tension: The classic three-chord cadence: tension from IV to V, release on I.
strings.Moves up the scale from IV to vi and end: Moves up the scale from IV to vi and ends on the dominant, which leads back to I.
strings.The iii chord adds a soft, wistful colou: The iii chord adds a soft, wistful colour on the way up to IV and V.
strings.A descending-fifths sequence in the styl: A descending-fifths sequence in the style of Pachelbel’s Canon; two chords per bar in the 4-bar form.
strings.The axis loop heard from its relative mi: The axis loop heard from its relative minor; a driving, modern pop and rock progression.
strings.Rising VI–VII lifts into the tonic (“hop: Rising VI–VII lifts into the tonic (“hopscotch” feel); the 8-bar form swaps the last VII for V.
strings.A stepwise descent in the bass; the majo: A stepwise descent in the bass; the major V (from harmonic minor) makes a strong pull back to i.
strings.A circle-of-fourths flavoured minor loop: A circle-of-fourths flavoured minor loop with the dark minor iv.
strings.Begins on the relative major, so it soun: Begins on the relative major, so it sounds hopeful before settling on the minor tonic.
strings.A classic minor cadence: the major V (ha: A classic minor cadence: the major V (harmonic minor) resolves back to i.
strings.The basic jazz cadence. At “Advanced” th: The basic jazz cadence. At “Advanced” the V7 may become an altered dominant or a tritone substitute (♭II7).
strings.The same cadence with ninth and thirteen: The same cadence with ninth and thirteenth extensions. Offered at Intermediate and Advanced level only.
strings.The most common jazz turnaround. At “Adv: The most common jazz turnaround. At “Advanced” tritone substitutions may replace V7.
strings.VI7 is the secondary dominant V7/ii lead: VI7 is the secondary dominant V7/ii leading to ii7; at “Advanced” it can be altered or replaced by its tritone substitute.
strings.A diminished seventh chord on the raised: A diminished seventh chord on the raised first degree connects I and ii chromatically.
strings.The diatonic circle-of-fifths sequence (: The diatonic circle-of-fifths sequence (“imperfect circle”) with a secondary dominant III7 returning to vi.
strings.Dominant-seventh blues harmony with a di: Dominant-seventh blues harmony with a diminished passing chord after IV7 and a ii–V turnaround; shortened from the 12-bar form.
strings.The “backdoor” approach to the tonic fro: The “backdoor” approach to the tonic from the minor iv and the dominant on ♭VII.
strings.Half-diminished ii and a dominant from h: Half-diminished ii and a dominant from harmonic minor; the V7 may carry ♭9 or alterations, or be tritone-substituted.
strings.The circle-of-fifths chain through the r: The circle-of-fifths chain through the relative major into a minor ii–V–i.
strings.A minor-key turnaround through the major: A minor-key turnaround through the major VI to the minor ii–V.
strings.Minor i and iv with a dominant seventh o: Minor i and iv with a dominant seventh on ♭VI moving to V7 before returning to i.
strings.diatonic sequence; major and minor ii–V–: diatonic sequence; major and minor ii–V–I

strings.ride on every beat and skip: ride on every beat and skip
strings.Hi-hat on every eighth, snare on 2 and 4: Hi-hat on every eighth, snare on 2 and 4, kick on 1 and 3. The Drum Ninja calls the hi-hat rock beat the most popular beat; the exact kick/snare placement shown is the common textbook version. The last eighth of the bar is an open hi-hat (common convention, not stated by the cited page).
strings.The Drum Ninja describes the popular pop: The Drum Ninja describes the popular pop beat as the rock beat with one extra kick just before the second snare (here: kick on the “and” of 3).
strings.Kick on every beat (stated by The Drum N: Kick on every beat (stated by The Drum Ninja and MasterClass). Open hi-hat on the off-beats (the classic disco/house “and” of every beat) and snare/clap on 2 and 4 are common conventions, not stated by those pages.
strings.The Drum Ninja: hi-hat in 16th notes (1: The Drum Ninja: hi-hat in 16th notes (1 e & a 2 e & a …), played evenly; here the in-between 16ths are softer for a natural feel. Kick/snare placement is a common choice.
strings.Half-time feel: the snare falls only on: Half-time feel: the snare falls only on beat 3 of the bar so the groove feels half as fast. This is a common convention (as is the open hi-hat at the end of the bar); it is not taken from a specific cited page.
strings.Ride cymbal plays the quarter-note pulse: Ride cymbal plays the quarter-note pulse plus a light skip note on the “and” of 2 and 4; hi-hat closed with the foot on 2 and 4; bass drum feathered very softly (Bonedo, The Instrumentalist). Swing is felt between a triplet and a tighter 16th feel, so 80 % is the default.
strings.The swing ride pattern plus sparse snare: The swing ride pattern plus sparse snare/kick accents; The Instrumentalist describes snare and bass drum accents played against the ride groove. The Charleston-style placement (kick on 1, soft snare on the “and” of 2) is a common convention, not stated by the source.
strings.The Drum Ninja lists a slow swing played: The Drum Ninja lists a slow swing played on ride and hi-hat with a swung feel; this version plays the skip note after every beat with a fully swung (triplet) feel.
strings.Simplified one-bar bossa nova: straight: Simplified one-bar bossa nova: straight eighths on the hi-hat, kick on 1, the “and” of 2, 3 and the “and” of 4, cross-stick (shown as soft snare) on 2 and 4. The NMEA sheet describes the bossa clave played with brushes; real bossa grooves span two bars, so this is an approximation.
strings.Swung eighth notes on the hi-hat with sn: Swung eighth notes on the hi-hat with snare accents on 2 and 4 (NMEA “Jazz Shuffle” sheet; The Drum Ninja lists the shuffle backbeat on 2 and 4). Kick on 1 and 3 is a common choice.

strings.Press “Generate Progression”. The chords: Press “Generate Progression”. The chords appear as bars. “Generate Another” gives you a new idea, “Reset” returns to the defaults.
strings.Press “Play” in the bar at the bottom. T: Press “Play” in the bar at the bottom. The progression repeats until you press “Stop”.
Open the Mixer with the “Mixer” button. Each part has a switch (Arp, Chords, Strums, Bass, Metro, Drums) and a volume fader.
strings.The buttons Player, Arp, Chords, Strums,: The buttons Player, Arp, Chords, Strums, Bass and Drums open the settings of each part above the bottom bar.
strings.Save your work with “Save progression”,: Save your work with “Save progression”, or export sound with “Export MIDI file” or “Export WAV file”.
strings.Play and Stop start and stop the playbac: Play and Stop start and stop the playback.
strings.Repeat plays the progression again and a: Repeat plays the progression again and again. Count-in plays leading bars first; their number is set in the Player panel.
strings.Tempo: use the slider or the buttons − a: Tempo: use the slider or the buttons − and + (one beat per minute per click).
The four circles show the current beat.
strings.Mixer: every part has its own switch and: Mixer: every part has its own switch and its own fader. “Master” sets the overall volume. “Metro” is the metronome.
strings.All parts are independent: block chords,: All parts are independent: block chords, strums, arpeggio, bass and drums can be switched on alone or in any combination.
strings.Style, length, mood, key and harmonic co: Style, length, mood, key and harmonic complexity steer the generator. “Simple” uses basic chords, “Advanced” also uses richer chords.
strings.Click a bar to edit its chords. Type up: Click a bar to edit its chords. Type up to four chords separated by spaces, for example C Am F G, and press Enter.
strings.In the edit field: Escape cancels, an em: In the edit field: Escape cancels, an empty field deletes the bar, and a vertical bar “|” splits the text into two bars.
strings.“Add bar” and “Remove last bar” change t: “Add bar” and “Remove last bar” change the length of the progression.
strings.“Show Roman numerals” shows the position: “Show Roman numerals” shows the position of each chord in the key (I, IV, V …).
strings.Chord notation in the header: Internatio: Chord notation in the header: International (B, B♭) or German (H, B). Language switches the whole page between English and German.
strings.Block chords play all notes of a chord a: Block chords play all notes of a chord at the same time. Switch them on with “Chords” in the Mixer; their settings are in the panel “Chords”.
strings.Sound: piano, organ, pad, strings, marim: Sound: piano, organ, pad, strings, marimba, steel or nylon guitar. A SoundFont can be loaded as well.
strings.Octave: the buttons − and + move the blo: Octave: the buttons − and + move the block chords up or down by whole octaves. This does not change any other part.
strings.Without the option “Play block chords in: Without the option “Play block chords in this rhythm” each chord is played once per chord change. With it, the chord is struck in the pattern of the matrix.
strings.Matrix: click a cell to switch it on, th: Matrix: click a cell to switch it on, then soft, then off. Each column is one sixteenth note.
strings.“Spread the notes slightly like a strum”: “Spread the notes slightly like a strum” is only for the sound steel or nylon guitar. It is off by default, so block chords stay real block chords.
strings.Guitar strumming is a separate layer wit: Guitar strumming is a separate layer with its own panel, matrix, switch (“Strums” in the Mixer), volume, octave and effects. It does not depend on the block chords.
strings.Every hit is played string by string in: Every hit is played string by string in standard tuning (E A D G B e). Common chords use the real guitar shapes, other chords use movable barre shapes or a calculated shape.
strings.Matrix, top row: click a cell to switch: Matrix, top row: click a cell to switch it on (filled dot), then soft (empty dot), then chuck (×), then off.
strings.A chuck is a muted stroke: the fretting: A chuck is a muted stroke: the fretting hand dampens the strings, and you hear a short percussive “chk”.
strings.Matrix, second row: the arrows show down: Matrix, second row: the arrows show down-strokes (↓) and up-strokes (↑). Click an arrow to flip the direction.
strings.Patterns: choose a ready-made guitar rhy: Patterns: choose a ready-made guitar rhythm, for example folk, pop, boom-chuck, or draw your own.
strings.Settings: strum speed, humanize, down-st: Settings: strum speed, humanize, down-stroke and up-stroke level, how many strings up-strokes play, pick attack (soft to hard) and ring-out (muted to ringing).
strings.Sound: built-in steel or nylon guitar, o: Sound: built-in steel or nylon guitar, or a SoundFont. The built-in sound has a guitar body and a short pick noise at the start of every stroke.
strings.You can save a strumming pattern as a fi: You can save a strumming pattern as a file (JSON with all settings, or a text file with rhythm and strokes) and load it again.
strings.The arpeggiator plays the notes of each: The arpeggiator plays the notes of each chord one after the other (fingerpicking). Switch it on with “Arp” in the Mixer.
strings.Matrix: each row is a tone of the chord: Matrix: each row is a tone of the chord (bass, root, 3rd, 5th, …), each column is one sixteenth note. Click a cell to switch it on, then soft, then off. Several rows in one column play together.
strings.Pattern: choose a ready-made picking pat: Pattern: choose a ready-made picking pattern or draw your own. Note length: one step, or ringing until the next hit.
strings.“Play the notes of the guitar chord shap: “Play the notes of the guitar chord shape” makes the rows the strings of the real guitar chord. Then you hear exactly what the tablature shows. This option is on by default.
strings.Octave: the buttons − and + move the arp: Octave: the buttons − and + move the arpeggio by whole octaves.
strings.Tablature: six lines for the strings e,: Tablature: six lines for the strings e, B, G, D, A, E (top to bottom). The numbers are fret numbers; 0 is an open string. Soft notes are shown in grey.
strings.“Chord shown” chooses the chord. “Follow: “Chord shown” chooses the chord. “Follows the playing chord” changes the display while the music plays. In a bar with two chords only the steps of the shown chord are filled.
strings.The chord diagram next to the tablature: The chord diagram next to the tablature shows the grip of the shown chord: × = string not played, ○ = open string, dots = fingers. For grips higher up the neck, the number of the first fret is written beside the diagram.
strings.“Export tablature as PNG” saves a pictur: “Export tablature as PNG” saves a picture of the tablature of the whole progression, four bars per line. You can give the file a name.
strings.The bass plays root, third, fifth, sixth: The bass plays root, third, fifth, sixth, seventh or octave of each chord in the low register. Switch it on with “Bass” in the Mixer.
strings.Rhythm: by default the bass follows the: Rhythm: by default the bass follows the kick drum. Choose “Own pattern” or edit any cell to draw your own bass rhythm.
strings.Sound: fingered, picked, acoustic or syn: Sound: fingered, picked, acoustic or synth bass, or a SoundFont.
strings.Octave: one octave down to two octaves u: Octave: one octave down to two octaves up. The bass is already very low, so one octave down can be hard to hear on small speakers.
strings.Choose the sound set (drum kit or cajon): Choose the sound set (drum kit or cajon), the genre, a ready-made rhythm and the time signature (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8).
strings.Pattern editor: click a cell to switch i: Pattern editor: click a cell to switch it on, then soft, then off. Each row has a round volume knob.
strings.Swing delays the off-beat notes for a sh: Swing delays the off-beat notes for a shuffled feel.
strings.Own WAV samples can replace the built-in: Own WAV samples can replace the built-in drum sounds.
strings.“Export drum groove” saves only the drum: “Export drum groove” saves only the drums as a MIDI or WAV file.
strings.Every part has round knobs under “Effect: Every part has round knobs under “Effects” at the top of its panel: Reverb (room sound) and Chorus (a wider, shimmering sound).
The drums have reverb only, no chorus.
strings.0 % means the effect is off. Use a littl: 0 % means the effect is off. Use a little: 10 to 30 % is often enough.
strings.Turn a knob by dragging up or down, with: Turn a knob by dragging up or down, with the mouse wheel, or with the keyboard: arrow keys change by 5, Page Up and Page Down by 10, Home sets 0 %, End sets 100 %. A double click or the Delete key resets it to 0 %.
strings.The effects are part of the WAV export,: The effects are part of the WAV export, but not of the MIDI export. The settings are kept only while the page stays open.
strings.Block chords, arpeggio, bass and strums: Block chords, arpeggio, bass and strums can each load their own SoundFont (a file ending in .sf2). Load the file, choose a preset, then choose “SoundFont” in the sound list of that part.
strings.Only plain .sf2 files work, not .sf3 or: Only plain .sf2 files work, not .sf3 or .sfz. The file stays on your computer and must be loaded again after every visit.
strings.Large SoundFonts need a lot of memory in: Large SoundFonts need a lot of memory in the browser. Small and medium files are safest.
strings.Own samples (WAV files named by note, fo: Own samples (WAV files named by note, for example piano_C4.wav) can be loaded in the Player panel.
strings.Save progression: saves the chords with: Save progression: saves the chords with key, time signature and tempo as a small file (JSON). A plain text file with chords such as C Am F G, one bar per line, can be loaded too. You can type a file name.
strings.Preset packs: a pack is a file with your: Preset packs: a pack is a file with your own presets. A preset can hold a progression plus arpeggio, bass, block chord rhythm and guitar strumming. You can create packs, add your current setup, save packs to a file and load packs from your computer.
strings.Export MIDI file: a standard MIDI file w: Export MIDI file: a standard MIDI file with separate tracks for chords, arpeggio, bass, strums and drums, for example for a DAW or notation program.
strings.Export WAV file: an audio file (16 bit): Export WAV file: an audio file (16 bit) with the sound of the app, including effects. Rendering takes a few seconds.
strings.The tick boxes in the export area decide: The tick boxes in the export area decide what is included: repeats, drums, count-in, block chords, arpeggio and bass.
strings.Everything can be used with the keyboard: Everything can be used with the keyboard: Tab moves forward, Shift+Tab backward, Enter or Space presses a button or switches a cell.
strings.In the matrices the arrow keys move from: In the matrices the arrow keys move from cell to cell.
strings.Escape closes an open panel and returns: Escape closes an open panel and returns to its button.
strings.Controls have text labels for screen rea: Controls have text labels for screen readers. The design is bright with strong contrast, and the panels fold up from the bottom bar so that the progression stays in view.
strings.No sound: check that the switch of the p: No sound: check that the switch of the part is on in the Mixer, that its fader is not at 0 %, and that the device volume is up. Browsers only start audio after a click, so press Play once.
strings.The message “Nothing to play”: switch on: The message “Nothing to play”: switch on at least one part in the Mixer.
strings.German or English does not switch: the l: German or English does not switch: the language files need the page to be opened from a web address (http or https). If the page is opened as a plain file from the computer, only English is available.
strings.A SoundFont does not load or sounds wron: A SoundFont does not load or sounds wrong: use a plain .sf2 file of moderate size and choose “SoundFont” in the sound list of the part.
strings.The page remembers your language and cho: The page remembers your language and chord notation. Preset packs stay in this browser until you remove them. Everything else is lost when the page is closed; save your progression to a file to keep it.
strings.Generate a progression to see the chord: Generate a progression to see the chord diagram.
strings.Standard tuning E A D G B e. Press a str: Standard tuning E A D G B e. Press a string to hear its reference tone, or switch the microphone on and pluck one string at a time.
{0} is too low: tighten the string.
{0} is too high: loosen the string.
strings.Play reference tone E, low string (6th): Play reference tone E, low string (6th)
strings.Play reference tone e, high string (1st): Play reference tone e, high string (1st)
strings.The microphone signal is analysed in you: The microphone signal is analysed in your browser only; nothing is recorded or sent anywhere. Works best in a quiet room with one string at a time. If the microphone is blocked, the reference tones still work.
strings.The microphone could not be used: permis: The microphone could not be used: permission denied or no microphone found. The reference tones still work.
strings.The microphone is not available in this: The microphone is not available in this browser (a secure https connection is required). The reference tones still work.
Audio is not available in this browser.
strings.“Play the notes of the guitar chord shap: “Play the notes of the guitar chord shape” makes the rows the strings of the real guitar chord, counted from the bass string: Bass string (thumb), then String 2 to String 6 upwards. If a chord shape has fewer strings, the upper rows start again from the lowest upper string, so no hit is silent. Then you hear exactly what the tablature shows. This option is on by default.
strings.Panning: under the fader of every part (: Panning: under the fader of every part (not Master) a round knob places the part in the stereo picture. “C” means centre, “L30” 30 % to the left, “R30” 30 % to the right. Drag the knob up or down, use the arrow keys (steps of 10 %), Home for fully left, End for fully right, double click or Delete for centre. Use headphones or two speakers.
strings.Chord diagram: at the bottom of the pane: Chord diagram: at the bottom of the panel the grip diagram shows the guitar shape that the strums play. “Chord shown” follows the playing chord or shows a chord of your choice.
strings.The tuner is in the bottom bar under “Tu: The tuner is in the bottom bar under “Tuner”. It helps you to tune the guitar to standard tuning (E A D G B e).
strings.Reference tones: press a string button (: Reference tones: press a string button (E, A, D, G, B, e) to hear its note for about four seconds. Press again to stop. Tune your string until it sounds the same.
strings.Microphone: press “Start microphone” and: Microphone: press “Start microphone” and allow the access when your browser asks. Pluck one string. The display shows the note, the frequency and how many cents (hundredths of a semitone) the string is too low or too high. Within ±5 cents it counts as in tune.
strings.The display is written out as text as we: The display is written out as text as well, so a screen reader announces the note and “too low”, “too high” or “in tune”.
strings.Reference pitch: the setting A4 (Hz) is: Reference pitch: the setting A4 (Hz) is 440 by default. Change it only if your ensemble tunes differently.
strings.Privacy: the microphone signal is analys: Privacy: the microphone signal is analysed in your browser only. Nothing is recorded or sent anywhere. The microphone is switched off when you close the panel.
strings.Limits: the microphone needs a secure we: Limits: the microphone needs a secure web address (https) and a quiet room. If the microphone is blocked, the reference tones still work. Play one string at a time; chords cannot be tuned this way.
strings.Count: the switch and the fader “Count”: Count: the switch and the fader “Count” set the count-in (the bars of clicks before the music starts). On a phone this is the quickest way to switch the count-in off; the same switch is in the Player panel. The count-in is independent of “Metro”: switch it off here if you do not want it.
strings.Load a SoundFont (.sf2) for block chords: Load a SoundFont (.sf2) for block chords
strings.Load a SoundFont (.sf2) for the arpeggio: Load a SoundFont (.sf2) for the arpeggio
strings.Load a SoundFont (.sf2) for the bass: Load a SoundFont (.sf2) for the bass
strings.Load a SoundFont (.sf2) for guitar strum: Load a SoundFont (.sf2) for guitar strumming
strings.Playing a short test groove with kick, h: Playing a short test groove with kick, hi-hat, snare and ride. Keys that the SoundFont does not contain use the built-in sound.
strings.Drums: choose “Drum sound source” = Soun: Drums: choose “Drum sound source” = SoundFont after loading a .sf2 file with a drum kit (usually bank 128). The rows are played with the General MIDI drum keys (kick 36, snare 38, hi-hat 42, open hi-hat 46, ride 51, percussion 54 to 69). Keys that the file does not contain use the built-in sound. The test button plays a short groove.
strings.Swing delays the “and” of every beat for: Swing delays the “and” of every beat for drums, block chords, strums, arpeggio and bass; the metronome stays straight.
strings.Swing delays the off-beat notes for a sh: Swing delays the off-beat notes for a shuffled feel. It acts on all instruments: drums, block chords, strums, arpeggio and bass. The metronome stays straight. Not used in 6/8.
strings.“Add bar” and “Remove last bar” change t: “Add bar” and “Remove last bar” change the length of the progression. Up to 32 bars are possible.
strings.Transpose: the buttons “−” and “+” next: Transpose: the buttons “−” and “+” next to Key move the whole progression one semitone down or up. The Key list follows (same mode), and all instruments, the tablature and the chord diagrams play and show the new key. Typed chords are transposed chord by chord. The number shows the semitones since the progression was generated; twelve steps lead back to the start. Choosing a key by hand starts the count again.
strings.“Play the notes of the guitar chord shap: “Play the notes of the guitar chord shape” makes the rows the real strings of the guitar chord: “Bass (lowest string)” is the thumb on the lowest string of the shape, the other rows are the A, D, G, B and e strings. If the shape does not use a string, the nearest string above it sounds, so no hit is silent. The ready-made patterns play the bass with the thumb and the G, B and e strings with the fingers. Then you hear exactly what the tablature shows. This option is on by default.
strings.Each song part (Intro, Verse, Chorus, Br: Each song part (Intro, Verse, Chorus, Bridge, Outro, End) keeps its own chords: choose the part under “Song part” in the Generator and create or type its chords. Here you list the parts in the order they are played and how often each is repeated. Then choose “Whole arrangement” under “What to play” in the Player panel: playing and the MIDI / WAV export follow this list. After the End part the last chord rings out.
strings.Saves all parts and the list in one smal: Saves all parts and the list in one small text file (JSON).
strings.The arrangement is empty, or all its par: The arrangement is empty, or all its parts have no chords yet. Add sections and give the parts chords.
strings.Playback stopped because the arrangement: Playback stopped because the arrangement changed.
strings.No part has chords yet. Choose a part un: No part has chords yet. Choose a part under “Song part” in the Generator and create its chords first.
strings.There is nothing to save yet: no part ha: There is nothing to save yet: no part has chords.
strings.the file is not a song of this app: the file is not a song of this app
strings.A song has six parts: Intro, Verse, Chor: A song has six parts: Intro, Verse, Chorus, Bridge, Outro and End. Each part has its own chords (up to 32 bars) and remembers the key it was made in.
strings.Choose the part under “Song part” in the: Choose the part under “Song part” in the Generator. Then “Generate Progression”, editing a bar, “Add bar” and Transpose work on that part only. The list shows how many bars each part has.
strings.Under “Song arrangement” you build the o: Under “Song arrangement” you build the order of the song: “Add section” appends the open part. For every line choose the part and how often it is repeated (1× to 16×). The arrows move a line, the cross removes it. “Standard order” fills the list with Intro, Verse ×2, Chorus ×2, Bridge, Chorus, Outro and End (only parts that have chords).
strings.In the Player panel choose “Whole arrang: In the Player panel choose “Whole arrangement” under “What to play”. Play then runs through the list; the display switches to the part that is playing and shows its repeat, for example “Chorus (2/2)”. “Repeat” in the bottom bar repeats the whole arrangement until the End part. “This part only” plays just the open part as before.
strings.The End part is the finish: when it has: The End part is the finish: when it has been played, the player stops by itself. The last chord rings out for one bar while the sound fades away, even when Repeat is on. Sections after the End part in the list are not played. The same ring-out is part of the MIDI and WAV export.
strings.MIDI and WAV export follow “What to play: MIDI and WAV export follow “What to play”: with “Whole arrangement” the whole song is exported (the MIDI file contains a marker for every section). The ring-out in the MIDI file is a held chord with a volume fade (CC 7).
strings.“Save song” stores all parts and the lis: “Save song” stores all parts and the list in one small file (JSON); “Load song” reads it back. Songs are loaded with the typed-chord format, so Roman numerals are computed again. A part that has no chords is skipped while playing.
strings.Tempo, time signature and the instrument: Tempo, time signature and the instrument settings are the same for all parts. Reset clears only the open part.
